title: AO/95/2016 of Smt. Babbo AND OTHERS Vs Pawan Arora AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Appeal from Order No. 92/2016
The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Ö. Appellant

Versus
Smt. Babbo & Others .Ö Respondents
Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Advocate, for the appellant.
Mr. Mohd. Azim, Advocate, for the claimants/respondents no. 1 to 5.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate, for the respondent no. 6.
With
Appeal from Order No. 95/2016
Smt. Babbo & Others Ö. Claimants/Appellants

Versus
Mr. Pawan Arora & Another .Ö Respondents
Mr. Mohd. Azim, Advocate, for the appellants/claimants.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate, for the respondent no. 1.
Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Advocate, for the respondent no. 2.

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Both these appeals titled above have arisen out of
the same judgment and order dated 2.12.2015 and the
learned Counsel of the parties have extensively been heard
by this Court at the stage of admission itself, hence are
being adjudicated finally as herein below.
The accident, as claimed, occurred on 30.5.2003 at
4 PM when the deceased Maksood Hussain, aged about 34
years, was travelling on his motorcycle no. UP21-L-0237,
he was dashed by another motorcycle borne youth Mr.
Pawan Arora, who was allegedly travelling on his own
motorcycle no. UP04-B-5461. This accident occurred on
Thakurdwara-Kashipur Road within the territorial
jurisdiction of Police Station Thakurdwara and the FIR was
lodged by Jabar Khan, brother of the deceased, on

2
1.6.2003 in the Police Station Thakurdwara. Maksood
Hussain became bitterly injured in the said accident and
he breathed his last while being shifted to the hospital.
The claim petition no. 367/2011 was instituted on
11.10.2011, i.e. almost after eight and half years of the
accident, by the dependants of Maksood Hussain claiming
compensation of rupees ten lakhs, whereagainst the
Tribunal granted Rs. 4,70,000/-.
The grant of compensation has been challenged by
the insurance company by filing the AO No. 92/2016, while
another AO No. 95/2016 has been preferred by the
claimants for enhancement of the award. Needless to say
that the motorcycle of Mr. Pawan Arora was insured by the
Oriental Insurance Company, the appellant herein.
Learned Counsel of the insurance company has
argued that Mr. Pawan Arora presented his written
statement before the Tribunal and denied any such
occurrence with the averment that this report could in fact
never be lodged in the police station, but Mr. Jabar Khan
with the planning of raising false claim against the
insurance company got received an application at the
police station with some illegible signatures of somebody.
Registration number of the motorcycle of Mr. Pawan Arora
was neither disclosed in the FIR nor in the claim petition
and even the name of Pawan Arora was not mentioned in
the FIR. No arrest of Pawan Arora was ever made nor any
prosecution was ever conducted against him.
Moreover, this claim petition has been filed with the
exorbitant delay of almost eight and half years after the
accident. It also indicates that no such accident ever took
place.
Learned Counsel on behalf of the insurance
company has also submitted that the Tribunal at Kashipur

3
did not have the territorial jurisdiction for the reason that
the so-called accident occurred within the territorial
jurisdiction of Police Station Thakurdwara, District
Moradabad. PW1 Smt. Babbo, the wife of the deceased, has
also mentioned her address in the witness box as the
resident of Village Shumalkhera, PS Dilari, District
Moradabad. So it can be inferred that just to create the
territorial jurisdiction of Kashipur Court, she has shown
her address through Mr. Jiyaul Hasan, resident of Village
Islamnagar Basai, Tehsil Kashipur, District Udham Singh
Nagar. However, no clarification or explanation was
furnished by her for this anomalous version.
Learned Counsel on behalf of the claimants has
drawn the attention of this Court towards a daily
newspaper cutting of Amar Ujala, paper no. 6Ga/6, which
reports that an accident of two motorcycles took place
resulting in death of Maksood Hussain and causing
injuries to two other persons. But this newspaper cutting,
firstly, is not admissible in the evidence and, secondly, it
has not been proved that this report is decisively of dated
31.5.2003 and how an illiterate woman Smt. Babbo along
with her minor children could be able to procure such
newspaper cutting which was published almost eight and
half years prior to filing the claim petition.
So, there is every possibility that this newspaper
report is not of 31.5.2003, but it was manipulated by
publishing somehow in the newspaper as a preparation of
filing the false petition for compensation just before
presentation of petition.
In view of what has been set forth above, I set aside
the impugned judgment and order. As a consequence, AO
No. 95/2016 filed by the claimants is dismissed and the AO

4
No. 92/2016 preferred by the insurance company is hereby
allowed.
Registry shall forthwith remit the compulsory
statutory amount, along with the interest it has earned, to
the Tribunal concerned. The money lying deposited by the
insurance, along with the interest accrued on it, and also
the amount so remitted by the Registry of this Court shall
be returned to the company immediately. The money
already released in favour of the claimants shall be
recoverable from them at the instance of insurance
company along with 6 per simple annual interest with
effect from the date of its release.
Let the LCR be sent back.
